_meta.axis: (3) angle dependence - which engine produces sigma(azimuth, elevation) for detection
_meta.author: subagent, read-only pass over existing ledgers + sionna 2.0.1 source
_meta.gpu_used: none - no new simulation was run; every number is read from an existing ledger or from the installed sionna source

A_source_audit_pathsolver.claim_under_test: PathSolver has no scattering integral - it only multiplies a Fresnel/Jones coefficient per path
A_source_audit_pathsolver.verdict: CONFIRMED, with one refinement: it is not only Fresnel, there is also an EMPIRICAL diffuse lobe, but there is still no aperture integral anywhere

evidence.reads: for every non-diffracted path the field is scaled by 1/(unfolded path length). No ray-tube curvature matrix (rho1,rho2), no divergence factor, therefore no dependence on the scatterer's size or curvature.
the whole channel coefficient is antenna_pattern x (product of Jones matrices) x lambda/(4 pi L). Nothing integrates over a surface.
the interaction is a 4x4 Jones matrix product - exactly the 'multiply a Fresnel coefficient' description.

diffuse reflection = sqrt(empirical scattering pattern f_s x MC ray-tube solid angle) x Fresnel magnitude. f_s is the Degli-Esposti lobe (lambertian/directive/backscattering, radio_materials/scattering_pattern.py) - a function of local incidence/scattering angle only, with no wavelength and no object extent in it.
no aperture/PO/Kirchhoff/induced-current term exists in the solver or the material layer.
stock default is specular+refraction+LOS only; diffuse must be switched on explicitly.

A_source_audit_pathsolver.consequence_for_angle: the amplitude of a path carries no information about how big the reflecting piece is, so a coherent lobe pattern produced by the target's aperture cannot arise. Azimuth can only enter through (i) the Fresnel coefficient vs local incidence angle (smooth), (ii) whether a flat facet's normal falls inside the specular acceptance window, (iii) Monte-Carlo sampling.

size_blindness.reads: specular channel obeys the infinite-mirror law (1/R^2, -19.9 dB/decade) and is exactly size-blind (slope ~1e-6 dB/decade). The diffuse channel does obey the radar law (~-40 dB/decade) but its absolute level is set by the free knob 'scattering_coefficient S'.

specular_channel_is_almost_always_empty.src_a: report15 specular_census.production (matrice4e, 8 az x 10 el x 4 rotor phase x 3 ranges = 960 cells, spp=2.048e9)
specular_channel_is_almost_always_empty.src_b: facet_count.json levels[0].spec_grid (mavic4pro, 12 az x 3 el = 36 aspects, spp=256e6)
specular_channel_is_almost_always_empty.reads: across the azimuth circle at el=0/15/90 the specular channel is identically zero except at az=0,el=0 (nose-on, normal incidence on the camera face). A pattern that is zero at 35 of 36 aspects is not an angle dependence.

curved_bodies_give_zero_specular.reads: a cylinder of 5 cm curvature radius returns 0 specular paths at 1/3/10 m no matter how finely it is tessellated. A drone is made of such radii, so the geometry-driven part of PathSolver's angle response is switched off for the airframe.

pec_sphere_gives_zero_paths.rows: r=0.3/1/3 m at spp=1e6 and 1.6e7 -> n_paths = 0 in all 6 runs

C_head_to_head_same_cells.scope: outputs/facet_count.json - mavic4pro, 3.5 GHz, R=10 m, el=+15 deg, bistatic 1.146 deg, az = 0/30/60/90 deg, production per-group materials, identical mesh for all three engines
C_head_to_head_same_cells.why_this_is_the_only_apples_to_apples_az: it is the ONLY ledger in outputs/ that runs stock Sionna PathSolver, our pure PO and our SBR at the same set of azimuths on the same mesh.

correlation_with_projected_area_over_the.reads: 4 points only - treat as a hint, not a test.

D_refutation_attempt_a_is_sionna_azimuth.question: PathSolver also moves when azimuth changes. Is that a lobe, or Monte-Carlo noise?
D_refutation_attempt_a_is_sionna_azimuth.answer: NEITHER OF THE TWO EASY ANSWERS. The movement is statistically real (so 'it is just MC noise' is FALSE and I retract that line of attack), but it is ~1.3 dB wide and it is an ENVELOPE, not an interference lobe pattern.

test_1_seed_null.reads: 3 seeds per azimuth. Between-azimuth variance beats seed variance by F=19.5 (incoherent). The azimuth dependence is real.

test_2_is_it_interference.method: decimate the mesh 30k -> 1.5k triangles (5 shape-valid rungs) and watch the azimuth pattern. A lambda=8.57 cm interference pattern cannot survive a 20x change in facet layout; a silhouette/Lambertian envelope can.
test_2_is_it_interference.reads: PathSolver's azimuth pattern is invariant to a 20x remesh (<=0.10 dB). Ours is not (0.4-2.3 dB in shape). Invariance to the facet layout is the signature of a geometric-optics envelope with no coherent aperture; sensitivity is the signature of interference. This is the cleanest available discriminator and it also names OUR cost: our lobe placement is mesh-dependent.

test_3_scale.caveat: our eps is over the full 360 deg circle at 3 deg; the Sionna 0.52 dB is over a quarter circle at 30 deg on a different drone. NOT the same statistic. But the gap is ~10x, far larger than any plausible sampling correction.
test_3_scale.reads: a published bistatic measurement puts the azimuth spread of a real airframe at 5.2-5.3 dB. Our kernel gives 4.0-6.5 dB (within -1.30/+1.16 dB). PathSolver's diffuse channel gives ~0.5 dB.

E_refutation_attempt_b_does_detection_ac.question: maybe one aspect-averaged sigma is enough and the lobe structure is decoration

finding_1_single_aspect_vs_36_azimuth_me.reads: quoting the nose-on value instead of the azimuth mean is worth -2.3 to +7.5 dB depending on airframe and band, i.e. up to a 1.53x error in detection range. So the angle axis is load-bearing for detection, not decoration.

finding_2_our_own_ledger_argues_the_othe.interpretation_quoted: 취약성의 주원인은 σ 의 '오차'가 아니라 '단일자세 인용'이다. σ 로브 구조가 밴드마다 완전히 재편되기 때문.
finding_2_our_own_ledger_argues_the_othe.reads: ⭐ THIS IS THE STRONGEST POINT AGAINST US. Our own robustness study concludes that quoting a single aspect is the main source of fragility and recommends the aspect-AVERAGED sigma for every headline claim. So the project does not, in fact, use the fine lobe structure - it averages it away.

E_refutation_attempt_b_does_detection_ac.why_the_axis_still_stands: the aspect mean is computed FROM sigma(azimuth). PathSolver produces no sigma at any azimuth (specular = size-blind mirror amplitude, zero at 35/36 aspects; diffuse = an arbitrary S knob), so it cannot produce the mean either. The honest competitor to our sigma(az) on this axis is a published measured sigma table, not PathSolver.
what_the_lobes_are_still_needed_for: Pd stated as a function of look angle (p10/p50/p90 across azimuth, not a single number)
the azimuth spread eps itself, which is the one angle quantity we can check against a measurement
the aspect mean, which cannot be formed without the pattern

F_our_kernel_lobe_structure_numbers.src: report13_sigma_grid.json (engine: sbr (rcs_sbr_batch, 1-bounce, penetrate=True), div=16, jitter=2, az step 3 deg x 120, el 23 rows, 3 bands, 7 airframes)
F_our_kernel_lobe_structure_numbers.warning_smoothing: meta.smooth_deg = 3.0 and sigma_dbsm is BIT-IDENTICAL to sigma_smooth_dbsm (checked: max|diff| = 0.0). The stored grid is already 3 deg smoothed - finer lobes than 3 deg are not in this file.
F_our_kernel_lobe_structure_numbers.reads: lobe count rises monotonically with carrier (median 17 at 1.843 GHz, 29 at 3.5 GHz, 34 at 5.21 GHz) - the signature of an interference pattern whose lobe width scales as lambda/D. Peak-to-peak is 15.4-31.2 dB, p90-p10 is 9.2-15.7 dB.

numerical_repeatability_floor.caveat_quoted: drone 자체의 dither 는 아직 안 쟀다 (ledger's own warning)
numerical_repeatability_floor.reads: a single sigma cell wobbles ~1.8 dB p-p when the ray grid is sub-cell shifted. Envelope statistics (p90-p10 ~ 9-16 dB) clear that floor by 5-9x; individual deep nulls (-36 to -41 dBsm) do not and must not be quoted.

detection_consequence.ptp_24.1_dB_same_cut: R90 moves 3.99x between best and worst azimuth

G_what_I_could_not_check: No fine-azimuth (<=5 deg) PathSolver sweep exists anywhere in outputs/. The finest Sionna azimuth sampling on record is 30 deg (facet_count.json, 12 az) and 45 deg (report15 specular census, 8 az). So I cannot MEASURE a PathSolver lobe period - I can only show, from the source and from the remesh-invariance test, that the mechanism for one is absent.
The 4-azimuth head-to-head is a single drone (mavic4pro), single range (10 m), single elevation (+15 deg), single band (3.5 GHz). It has not been repeated.
The drone's own SBR dither (numerical repeatability of a sigma cell on a drone rather than a PEC sphere) is unmeasured - the ledger says so explicitly.

PathSolver's diffuse channel absolute level depends on the per-material scattering_coefficient S. rt_no_rcs_verify.json B_sphere_S shows the returned level moving from -12.79 dB to +2.97 dB relative to truth as S goes 0.2 -> 1.0. I did not audit which S our production materials use, so I cannot say how far off the diffuse azimuth envelope's absolute level is.

I did not check elevation as carefully as azimuth. Our grid has 23 elevation rows; the ledger warns el=-90 is a degenerate row (one sigma replicated over azimuth) and must not be used for azimuth statistics.
